Great day trip with Parkbus (also easy to navigate solo using the AllTrails map). Plenty of scenic viewpoints along the Niagara Escarpment — dramatic cliffs and great bird-watching (lookout for Turkey Vultures).. Trails are generally easy for regular hikers but can be challenging for first-timers because of rocky and steeper sections. Bring sunscreen, a rain jacket or umbrella, lunch, plenty of water, and insect repellent. Crawford Lake is currently closed for renovations, but if the reconstructed village is open, definitely visit — ask the guides for details, it really heightens the experience. Stay back from the cliff edges and pack out your trash
The trail was in great condition. There was one section that was muddy but the rest was dry. Lots of tree coverage on the entire trail. The elevation provided a good challenge!

Very well maintained. I extended my route to include a couple of different trail segments. All in all we got over 15 km in. Definitely some steep climbs especially if you’re treating it as a loop on the way back you will see those towards the parking lot. One thing that sort of put me off is why they are charging so much money per person instead of per vehicle. But as far as cleanliness, I must admit I probably saw one or two pieces of litter. the bathrooms are basically an outhouse you’re better off going in the woods bugs were not bad first week in September, they got worse as dusk approached around 5 PM.

when we were there, there was at least one muddy section that could really use a bridge or stones. I don't know if it's always like this, but it will muck up your shoes if you don't pick your steps very carefully. don't slip! 

otherwise it was very beautiful, lots of up & down climbing. 

I only wish I knew that the peak of rattlesnake is accessible by car, and has quite a large parking lot, which means there was  a large crowd there to enjoy the beautiful fall colors. for me, it dulled the enjoyment of the hike and I preferred earlier lookout points since I didn't have to hear yelling, crowd noises or wait my turn to walk to the edge. I would advise doing the hike earlier in the day  for that reason!

Started at Crawford Lake, hiked to Rattlesnake Point Conservation & back. 
Lots of parking at Crawford and opportunities to add on some more KMs with their trail system as well if you want. 
The hike is basically down into the a Nassagaweya Canyon & back up the other side, out to Rattlesnake & then back through the canyon again. 
The uphill parts of the canyon are fairly steep, rocks to avoid in places & some mud. a well maintained trail but won’t be accessible to all. Rocky, tree roots & narrow in places. 
Good hike. Works the cardio on those uphills. 
Mosquitoes a plenty first thing in the morning but bug spray held them at bay.

We had our lunch we packed and turned around and headed back. 

Some how it seemed even muddier on the way back since it was warmer. 

We kept putting on and taking our icers off. Or we would have lost them in the mud. Some muddy areas were probably few inches deep. But what fun and the calories burned. 

On the way back to the car, half the cars were gone. 

We just felt relief we were done. The extra work from the muddy areas just wore us out.
